n: Paul closes by introducing Phebe, the likely carrier of this letter to Rome. She served the church in Cenchrea, the eastern port of Corinth, where Paul was writing.

f.g: Greek diakonos — one who serves or ministers; the same word behind “deacon.”
A harbor town about seven miles east of Corinth, on the Saronic Gulf.

n: Paul asks the Roman saints to welcome Phebe as fellow believers should and to help her with whatever she needs. She had generously supported many people, Paul included.

f.g: As is fitting for saints — the way Church members ought to treat one another.
Helper, patron, protector; someone who used her means to support others.

n: Priscilla and her husband Aquila were tentmakers who had worked and lived with Paul in Corinth and Ephesus. Now back in Rome, they are some of his most trusted partners.
At some point this couple risked their lives to protect Paul. Gentile congregations everywhere were grateful to them for keeping the apostle safe.

f.g: An idiom: they put their own lives on the line, as if offering their necks to the executioner.

n: Early Christians met in private homes, and a congregation gathered in Priscilla and Aquila’s house. Epaenetus was one of the very first converts in his region.

f.w: the church that is in their house

f.g: Many manuscripts read “Asia”; either way, he was among the first converts there, like the first harvest offered to God.

n: A woman named Mary had worked hard for the believers. Paul remembers individual service by name, showing how much he valued every disciple’s labor.

f.g: Worked hard, toiled — a word Paul often uses for gospel service.

n: Andronicus and Junia were fellow Jews who had been imprisoned with Paul. They had joined the Church before Paul’s own conversion and were well respected by the apostles.

f.g: Probably fellow Israelites rather than close family.

n: Paul sends love to Amplias (Ampliatus), a name common among slaves and freedmen in Rome. In the Lord, social rank made no difference to Paul’s affection.
Urbane (Urbanus) worked alongside Paul in spreading the gospel, and Stachys was another dear friend. The list shows how wide Paul’s network of friendships was.

f.g: Greek synergos — fellow worker, co-laborer.

n: Apelles had proven faithful through trials. Paul also greets the believers in the household of Aristobulus, which may have included servants of a prominent family.

f.g: Tested and proven genuine, like metal that has passed the refiner’s test.
Some scholars think this was the household of Aristobulus, a grandson of Herod the Great who lived in Rome.

n: Herodion was a fellow Jew. Paul greets the Christians among the household of Narcissus — likely servants in a large Roman household — specifying those who were believers.

f.g: Only some of the household were Christians; Paul greets those who were.

n: Tryphena and Tryphosa, perhaps sisters, worked diligently in the Lord’s service, as did a beloved woman named Persis. Many women were key workers in the early Church.
Rufus was a choice disciple, and his mother had cared for Paul like a mother of his own. Some think Rufus was a son of Simon of Cyrene, who carried Jesus’ cross.

f.g: She had treated Paul with a mother’s care.

n: Paul greets a group of men and the believers who met with them — perhaps another house congregation in Rome.

f.w: the brethren which are with them
f.g: Probably those who worshiped together in one home-based group.

n: Another circle of believers, including a woman named Julia and Nereus’s sister. Rome’s Church was made up of many small gatherings scattered around the city.

f.g: “Saints” in the New Testament means all baptized members of the Church, not only exceptionally holy people.

n: A kiss on the cheek was a common greeting of affection in that culture. Paul asks the saints to greet one another with sincere, holy love, and sends greetings from the other congregations.
Paul warns the saints to watch out for people who stir up division and lead others into sin by teaching things contrary to the gospel they were taught — and to keep away from them.

f.g: Watch closely, keep an eye on.

n: Such people are not serving Christ but their own appetites and interests. With smooth talk and flattery they fool those who are innocent and trusting.

f.g: Their own desires and selfish gain.
The unsuspecting or naive, not the unintelligent.

n: The Roman saints’ faithfulness was known everywhere, and Paul rejoices over it. Still, he wants them to be wise and skilled at goodness, but innocent and inexperienced in evil.

f.w: wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil

n: Echoing God’s first promise in Eden that the woman’s seed would crush the serpent’s head, Paul assures them that God will soon give them victory over Satan.
Paul’s companions with him in Corinth add their greetings, including young Timothy, his close missionary companion, and several fellow Jews.

f.g: Timothy, Paul’s trusted companion and later the recipient of two letters.

n: Tertius, the scribe who actually wrote down the letter as Paul dictated it, adds his own greeting. Paul commonly used scribes for his letters.

f.g: Paul dictated; a secretary (amanuensis) wrote.

n: Gaius was hosting Paul and opened his home to the whole congregation. Erastus, the city treasurer of Corinth, also sends greetings — a sign that the gospel reached people of influence.

f.g: Steward or treasurer of the city.

n: Paul repeats his blessing of grace. Many early manuscripts lack this verse, but its words match Paul’s usual farewell.

f.w: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ

n: Paul closes with praise to God, who can make the saints strong and steady. The gospel is the “mystery” — God’s plan once hidden but now openly revealed through Jesus Christ.

f.g: Establish; make firm and steady.
In Paul’s writing, a sacred truth that can only be known by revelation.

n: That plan is now made known to all nations, and the prophets’ writings confirm it. Its purpose is to bring people to the obedience that flows from faith.
The letter ends with a doxology — a short hymn of praise — giving glory forever to the only wise God through Jesus Christ.
